correctness.rationale: An independent count avoids relying on the supplied enumerator. Subsets of size at most two have identical induced-edge distributions in both graphs. For a k-set in a cubic graph of order six, e(S)-e(V\S)=3(k-3), so sizes at least four also agree. For three-sets the counts at 0,1,2,3 edges have the same zeroth, first and second binomial moments (20 triples, 36 incidences of an edge in a triple, and 18 wedges). The third moment differs by two because the prism has exactly two triangles and the biclique none. Back substitution gives the difference (-2,6,-6,2), hence the stated polynomial and all cumulative differences. The biclique's 15 independent sets and 9 one-edge sets give 24 at threshold one, so the prism gives 28. Complements of simple cubic graphs at order six are exactly the cycle types (6) and (3,3), giving the prism and the biclique. The only smaller positive admissible order for d>=2 and 2d|n has (d,n)=(2,4), with the unique graph C4. Carenini's inclusive cutoff equals one at the stated parameters. This proof reconstructs the census and threshold profile for simple graphs without executing the deposited code.
residual_risks: The complete census is for simple graphs; no extension to a multigraph convention or to larger orders is implied.
